dialogues.speaker: Furuya Noboru
dialogues.text: Why, if it isn't a new rookie!

dialogues.speaker: Furuya Noboru
dialogues.text: *cough* Welcome! Feel free to ask me if you have any questions.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You look pretty pale. Are you okay?

dialogues.speaker: Furuya Noboru
dialogues.text: It's okay. I was just born with a weak constitution. *cough* Thank you for asking.

dialogues.speaker: Furuya Noboru
dialogues.text: I have been weak and prone to sickness since I was little. I joined the Adventurers' Guild after I had grown up, hoping to train my body through adventures.

dialogues.speaker: Furuya Noboru
dialogues.text: Although I have gathered quite a lot of experience, my body still remains the same... Oh, no no... I'm not some great adventurer worth mentioning or anything.

dialogues.speaker: Furuya Noboru
dialogues.text: However, because I have been in Inazuma for so long, I happen to know more about the local Adventurers' Guild than anyone else. *cough* If you have any questions, feel free to ask me anytime.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm afraid I'm no longer a rookie.

dialogues.speaker: Furuya Noboru
dialogues.text: Wow, such forcefulness! It seems that I have judged a book by its cover. My apologies.

dialogues.speaker: Furuya Noboru
dialogues.text: But since you have just arrived in Inazuma, you probably still find many things unfamiliar. If you run into any trouble, be careful. Come look for me!

dialogues.speaker: Furuya Noboru
dialogues.text: Inazuma is in turmoil right now, which you probably already know. However, this may be a blessing in disguise. Ever since the Sakoku Decree, fewer and fewer foreign adventurers have been arriving, so there should still be quite a lot of lost treasures to be found.

dialogues.speaker: Furuya Noboru
dialogues.text: If you have confidence in your abilities, this might be the right place for you to flex your muscles.

dialogues.speaker: Furuya Noboru
dialogues.text: *cough* Anyway, best you be careful when going outside. The Adventurers' Guild will always be behind you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye! Take care of yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Furuya Noboru
dialogues.text: Thanks! You too, young adventurer!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Tell me about Inazuma...

dialogues.speaker: Furuya Noboru
dialogues.text: You want to know more about the geography of Inazuma? Ahem... No problem!

dialogues.speaker: Furuya Noboru
dialogues.text: I figure that you must've come to Narukami Island from Ritou through Konda Village, right? Then I need not mention them, though there are some urban legends about Byakko Plain, which is also on that path. Who knows if those are true or not?

dialogues.speaker: Furuya Noboru
dialogues.text: To the north of Inazuma City, you will find the Grand Narukami Shrine on the mountaintop. The great Sacred Sakura tree at the shrine is a truly spectacular sight.

dialogues.speaker: Furuya Noboru
dialogues.text: Beneath the Grand Narukami Shrine are Mt. Yougou and the Chinju Forest. It's very difficult to climb Mt. Yougou. There are also legends about bake-danuki running amok in the Chinju Forest. Be extra careful if you go there.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's outside Narukami Island?

dialogues.speaker: Furuya Noboru
dialogues.text: Outside of Narukami Island, if you keep going southwest, you will find Kannazuka, Tatarasuna and Yashiori Island.

dialogues.speaker: Furuya Noboru
dialogues.text: These islands have been the focus of recent military conflicts, and I don't recommend that adventurers go there alone. However, many could not resist the temptation of treasure hunting... *cough*

dialogues.speaker: Furuya Noboru
dialogues.text: In addition, I haven't heard much good about the Mikage Furnace of Tatarasuna at Kannazuka... Anyway, those who can't handle themselves well had best stay away from these places for now.

dialogues.speaker: Furuya Noboru
dialogues.text: After passing through these islands, you will find yourself in the most remote corner of Inazuma, Watatsumi Island, a place under the jurisdiction of the Sangonomiya.

dialogues.speaker: Furuya Noboru
dialogues.text: Further down... you will be in southern Inazuma. This is a place that is constantly shrouded by fog. It sure doesn't look like anything good from this side of the ocean...

dialogues.speaker: Furuya Noboru
dialogues.text: While I'm curious about what exactly is hiding in the thick fog, I wouldn't suggest going there.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's outside Narukami Island?

dialogues.speaker: Furuya Noboru
dialogues.text: Outside of Narukami Island, if you keep going southwest, you will find Kannazuka, Tatarasuna and Yashiori Island.

dialogues.speaker: Furuya Noboru
dialogues.text: These islands have been the focus of recent military conflicts, and I don't recommend that adventurers go there alone. However, many could not resist the temptation of treasure hunting... *cough*

dialogues.speaker: Furuya Noboru
dialogues.text: In addition, I haven't heard much good about the Mikage Furnace of Tatarasuna at Kannazuka... Anyway, those who can't handle themselves well had best stay away from these places for now.

dialogues.speaker: Furuya Noboru
dialogues.text: After passing through these islands, you will find yourself in the most remote corner of Inazuma, Watatsumi Island, a place under the jurisdiction of the Sangonomiya.

dialogues.speaker: Furuya Noboru
dialogues.text: You can find Tsurumi Island to the south of Inazuma. That place has always been shrouded in fog, but that fog has dissipated suddenly for some reason...

dialogues.speaker: Furuya Noboru
dialogues.text: The Shogunate has no doubt noticed this as well. I've heard that they're planning to send people to develop that land after an observational period.

dialogues.speaker: Furuya Noboru
dialogues.text: Ah, right. While the fog may be gone, the situation is still unclear for now. I would probably still advise any new adventurers to not go there willy-nilly.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm afraid I'm no longer a rookie.

dialogues.speaker: Furuya Noboru
dialogues.text: Wow, such forcefulness! It seems that I have judged a book by its cover. My apologies.

dialogues.speaker: Furuya Noboru
dialogues.text: But since you have just arrived in Inazuma, you probably still find many things unfamiliar. If you run into any trouble, be careful. Come look for me!

dialogues.speaker: Furuya Noboru
dialogues.text: Still, I expect that there'll be competition for all the buried treasure soon, what with the number of adventurers we're expecting to arrive at our shores from overseas soon.

dialogues.speaker: Furuya Noboru
dialogues.text: If you have confidence in your abilities, this might be the right place for you to flex your muscles.

dialogues.speaker: Furuya Noboru
dialogues.text: *cough* Anyway, best you be careful when going outside. The Adventurers' Guild will always be behind you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Duel

dialogues.speaker: Furuya Noboru
dialogues.text: It seems I've lost... Hmm... I didn't realize where the game started to go wrong...

dialogues.speaker: Furuya Noboru
dialogues.text: Hmm... Beginners always seem to make the same mistakes...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I look forward to working with you.

dialogues.speaker: Furuya Noboru
dialogues.text: Seeing as you've just arrived, I'll share with you some of the experiences that I've gathered over the years.

dialogues.speaker: Furuya Noboru
dialogues.text: In this rapidly changing world, I think there'll always be situations where the experience may be of use to you.
